subject: FRE
label: Grade 09
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 09 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Near future, recent past and present continuous
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Near future, recent past and present continuous', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: use these forms. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Near future, recent past and present continuous' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use these forms, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Je vais manger (near future). Je viens de manger (recent past). Je suis en train de manger (present continuous). Method: Model run for 'Near future, recent past and present continuous'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Use these forms: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, The near future uses aller plus the infinitive. Je vais partir demain. [I am going to leave tomorrow.] Nous allons visiter le musée. [We are going to visit the museum.] Conjugate aller correctly: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont.

Step 2, The recent past uses venir de plus the infinitive. Je viens de manger. [I have just eaten.] Elle vient d'arriver. [She has just arrived.] Conjugate venir: je viens, tu viens, il vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils viennent.

Step 3, The present continuous uses être en train de plus the infinitive. Je suis en train de lire. [I am in the middle of reading.] Ils sont en train de jouer. [They are playing right now.] It stresses that the action is happening at this moment.

Step 4, Dialogue. Maman : Tu viens de finir tes devoirs ? [Have you just finished your homework?] L'enfant : Non, je suis en train de les faire. [No, I am doing them.] Maman : Et après ? [And afterwards?] L'enfant : Après, je vais jouer au foot. [Afterwards I am going to play football.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says je viens de mangé. Correction: je viens de manger, with the infinitive. Another says je vais de partir. Correction: je vais partir, with no de. A third says je suis en train lire; correction: je suis en train de lire.

Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence with each form about a trip. Model answer: Nous allons partir à la mer. Je viens de préparer ma valise. Maman est en train de réserver les billets. [We are going to leave for the sea. I have just packed my case. Mum is in the middle of booking the tickets.]

modules.title: Comparing education systems
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Comparing education systems', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: compare two systems. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Comparing education systems' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: compare two systems, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: En France l'ecole elementaire commence a six ans, puis le college, puis le lycee. Fais un tableau: age, annees, examens, une ressemblance et une difference avec ton systeme. Method: Model run for 'Comparing education systems'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Compare two systems: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Collect facts in two columns. In France: école primaire five years (ages 6 to 11), collège four years (11 to 15), lycée three years (15 to 18), ending with the baccalauréat. For comparison use an invented system B: six years of primary, three of lower secondary, three of upper secondary. Total in both: 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 and 6 + 3 + 3 = 12.

Step 2, Learn the comparison forms. plus ... que [more ... than], moins ... que [less ... than], aussi ... que [as ... as]. Le primaire est plus long dans le système B qu'en France. [Primary school is longer in system B than in France.] Les deux systèmes durent aussi longtemps. [Both systems last as long.]

Step 3, Link ideas with contrast words. alors que, tandis que [whereas], par contre [on the other hand], en revanche [in contrast]. En France, le collège dure quatre ans, alors que dans le système B le premier cycle du secondaire dure trois ans. [In France lower secondary lasts four years, whereas in system B it lasts three.]

Step 4, Add a similarity and an opinion. Dans les deux systèmes, les élèves passent douze ans à l'école. [In both systems, pupils spend twelve years at school.] À mon avis, un collège plus long permet de mieux préparer le lycée. [In my opinion a longer collège prepares better for lycée.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says plus bon. Correction: meilleur, since bon has an irregular comparative. Another says aussi long comme. Correction: aussi long que. Another writes Le système est plus longue. Correction: plus long, because système is masculine. Check agreement.

Step 6, Your turn: compare country A with five school days of 8 hours and country B with four school days of 8 hours. Answer: Dans le pays A, les élèves sont à l'école 40 heures par semaine, alors que dans le pays B ils y sont 32 heures. La semaine est donc plus longue dans le pays A.

modules.title: Personal pronouns y and en
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Personal pronouns y and en', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: use y and en. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Personal pronouns y and en' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use y and en, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: In 'The dog lives in Lyon, in France', 'dog' is a common noun, 'Lyon' and 'France' are proper nouns and need capital letters. Method: Model run for 'Personal pronouns y and en'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Use y and en: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, The pronoun y replaces à plus a place or thing. Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'y vais. [Are you going to Paris? Yes, I am going there.] Il pense à son voyage. Il y pense. [He thinks about his trip. He thinks about it.] Y goes before the verb.

Step 2, The pronoun en replaces de plus a noun or a quantity. Tu veux du pain ? Oui, j'en veux. [Do you want some bread? Yes, I want some.] Elle vient de Lyon. Elle en vient. [She comes from Lyon. She comes from there.] J'ai deux frères. J'en ai deux. [I have two brothers. I have two.]

Step 3, Position rules. With the near future the pronoun goes before the infinitive: Je vais y aller. [I am going to go there.] In the negative: Je n'y vais pas. Je n'en veux pas. [I am not going there. I do not want any.] The pronoun stays next to its verb.

Step 4, Dialogue. Élève A : Tu es allé au cinéma ? [Did you go to the cinema?] Élève B : Oui, j'y suis allée hier. [Yes, I went there yesterday.] Élève A : Tu as pris des chips ? [Did you get some crisps?] Élève B : Oui, j'en ai pris. [Yes, I got some.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says Je en veux. Correction: J'en veux, with elision. Another says J'en ai deux frères. Correction: J'en ai deux, because en already replaces frères. A third says Je vais à y aller; correction: Je vais y aller.

Step 6, Your turn: rewrite with y or en. Elle va à l'école. Nous avons trois chats. Je ne veux pas de lait. Model answer: Elle y va. Nous en avons trois. Je n'en veux pas. [She goes there. We have three. I do not want any.]

modules.title: Culture and civilisation
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Culture and civilisation', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: describe aspects of French-speaking cultures. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Culture and civilisation' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe aspects of French-speaking cultures, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: La Francophonie: le francais est parle sur plusieurs continents (France, Canada, Senegal). Choisis un pays francophone et presente trois faits. Method: Model run for 'Culture and civilisation'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Describe aspects of French-speaking cultures: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Locate French-speaking places. French is spoken by hundreds of millions of people on five continents. Countries with French as an official language include la France, la Belgique, la Suisse, le Canada, le Sénégal and la Côte d'Ivoire. Use en with feminine countries and au with masculine ones: en France, au Canada, au Sénégal.

Step 2, Describe languages and everyday facts. La Suisse a quatre langues nationales : l'allemand, le français, l'italien et le romanche. [Switzerland has four national languages.] Au Québec, la langue officielle est le français. [In Quebec, the official language is French.] Use est and a to give facts.

Step 3, Describe festivals and food. En France, la fête nationale est le 14 juillet. [In France the national day is 14 July.] Au Québec, la fête nationale est le 24 juin. En Belgique, on mange des frites et des gaufres. En Suisse, on mange de la fondue. Au Québec, on mange de la poutine.

Step 4, Write a short description. Au Sénégal, le français est une langue officielle, mais beaucoup de gens parlent aussi le wolof. [In Senegal French is an official language, but many people also speak Wolof.] Use on and il y a to describe general customs without needing exact names.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child writes Je vais en Canada. Correction: au Canada. Another says La Suisse a trois langues. Correction: quatre. Another uses capital letters: Français, Juillet. Correction: le français is a language and juillet a month, both written with small letters.

Step 6, Your turn: describe one French-speaking country in three sentences. Model answer: La Belgique est un pays en Europe. On y parle français, néerlandais et allemand. On y mange des frites et des gaufres. [Belgium is a country in Europe. French, Dutch and German are spoken there. People eat chips and waffles there.]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
